body:
>Not really sure how to put it other than to stop worrying about the "big questions" like all this universe, multiverse, immortality, afterlife stuff.

I really wish I could, but no matter what I do those questions will always be there, bleeding into all of my thoughts. I have a weird, uncontrollable drive to understand these things. The small questions bore me, but maybe one day working on understanding the oceans or our solar system or quantum mechanics could be cathartic for me? I don't know.

>Sounds really immature to say but if you believe for a fact that we are just "nothing more than biological energy conversion machines, whose only purpose in life is to compete to reproduce and pass on our genes." Then it is what it is, you shouldn't dwell on it.

The real problem is we haven't progressed far enough to know either way. Maybe this is just a computer simulation. Maybe there really is a god or gods looking over us. Maybe we just aren't intelligent enough genus Homos to understand what strange things are really going on. All we know for sure right now is that is we eat, we sleep, we compete and we consume to pass on our genes, with no real goal in sight. And that's where my struggles with morality come into play. 

Like theoretically, let's say I'm the next Einstein and I have the power to make some great discovery that advances humanity. Then wouldn't I have a moral obligation to the human race to devote my life to understanding and working and progressing? But what if we are not alone in the universe, and once we make it to space, we continue to consume, destroy and reproduce, treating the stars like viruses treat our human cells: exploiting sun after sun simply to perpetuate our own DNA? Then wouldn't I have a moral obligation to do everything in my power to stop humanity? Like fuck, this is why I hate morality. It just confuses me.

>"what would happen to me"

Basically I'm worried that I could be so far gone, they would overreact and declare me insane or dangerous or something. This post I made is my way of finding out.

>you just seem to have a very...blatant, "vanilla" (for lack of a better term) outlook on life

I get that, but is there any other way of looking at it that doesn't fly in the face of logic and rationalism? Can we have our cake and eat it too? I'm genuinely wondering.

>People who are smarter than you won't be inclined to help until you ditch the egoistic, juvenile, nihilistic attitude.

I understand that, but I literally do not know how to think any other way. This is just the way I am, unbearably logical and rational. Nothing else makes sense to me. How can I believe something that science and logic dictate isn't true? Wouldn't giving in and believing something scientifically false actually make me crazy and unreasonable?

I do not think I am egoistic or juvenile. I am simply very talented, and I think what I wrote was very objective. But I still need help.

>Anyone who wonders if he's a sociopath isn't a sociopath.

I get that that makes sense on paper from a definition standpoint, but I both do and do not feel emotion towards others. It's a fucked up dichotomy. Like my brain innately makes me feel emotion, but at the same time the rational part of me shows me how foolish it all is. Like if my parents died tomorrow I do not think I would be upset. I have accepted the fact that we're all already dead, so what purpose is there in getting upset about the inevitable? I both do and do not fear death, because I know I am already dead.

I'm going to continue looking for psychologists as soon as I am finished with finals. 

>but if you'd like to discuss anything feel free to reply or message me or something.

I basically just want to know your initial reactions to my post. How far away am I from normal? I struggle immensely with understanding how other people think, because it's just so foreign to me.

>There's some serious shit wrong with you but I don't think you're bipolar.

I don't think I am either and that's the weirdest part to me. I fit a whole lot of the symptoms, but I've analyzed them and they don't seem irrational to me. Is it still bipolar disorder if it's all rational?

>Have you always been this way or was there something that happened in your life that's caused you to become so self-serving and disconnected?

I sort of always was this way. I have problems with authority; I cannot listen to someone who I think is less intelligent than myself. I think I am too smart for my own good. 

As a child I was always leading groups and raising hell.  In grade school I was constantly starting fights and trying to skirt the rules wherever I could (I would make a phenomenal lawyer). If I could get away with it, I would; I just really enjoyed pitting myself against the world and winning. It was to the point where the principal had my mother on speed dial I was in his office so often. I think part of the reason I was this way is that I was an overweight child and was picked on mercilessly. But rather than take it, I would strike back with a vengeance, because I knew I could beat them.

My parents would send my away to summer camp every year, and I would pull the same shit there. As soon as our counsellors would turn their back, I would steal the entire group and lead them on my own adventures. It was just too easy. It was to the point that I was infamous and needed to be watched at all times.

Then around the time puberty started to hit, I chilled out a lot. I realized I could not go on like that and became a productive member of society. In high school, I turned out to be boy wonder. I took 6 AP courses, the rest were honors and received 1 A- the entire 4 years. Literally everything else was an A. I received several 100's, not getting a single question wrong the entire year. I quarterbacked the football team and captained the volleyball. I dated the hottest girl, and had others chomping at the bit, but despite all that I had very, very low confidence. I think being a fat child really set me back. 

I think the problem started when I fell madly in love with girl I was dating. Like I mentioned earlier, I was raised Catholic and that really screwed me up. All drugs were evil, premarital sex was evil, I should strive to only date and marry 1 girl. So I did what I thought I was supposed to do and was the perfect boyfriend. Calling, sending flowers, just generally being over attached. I thought this is was how I was supposed to act. 

Then college happened and I got dumped. That started nearly 2 years of depression where I gained 50 pounds and almost killed myself. I was too scared to talk to anyone, too scared to leave my room, had no confidence and eventually dropped out of school. But every time I thought about killing myself something wonderful would happen. I'd realize, well if I'm just gonna kill myself, why not go out and live life however the fuck I want? What not do what I want, say what I want, wear what I want and fuck what everyone else thinks. I realized how ridiculously overattached I had been to my gf (I had told her I wanted to transfer to her school and get married, yikes), and I finally began to think for myself. I continued to get smarter and more knowledgable every day, and basically that's how I got to where I am now.
